# PR #3961: Patch: the daily board shows no 60-second countdown on KY's Competition's questions

Closes #3839

On the daily board, a KY's Competition (Meditative+ #20) question no longer shows the 60-second countdown (R3727003). A live match and practice still show it (R1563006). The move's daily clock pill was already on the board, so it stays as the only clock.

## What changed
- **`Prompt.tsx`**: a new optional `sequenceClock` prop on `Prompt` and on the engine picker. It defaults to true. The `SequenceCountdown` render is gated on it, outside the component, so no hook is called conditionally. `SequenceCountdown` and `sequenceClock.ts` are unchanged.
- **`Game.tsx`**: a `sequenceClock` prop that defaults to `true` and passes through to `<Prompt>`.
- **`DailyBoard.tsx`**: passes `sequenceClock={false}` to `<Game>`, and the file header says why.
- **`spec/rulings/R3727003.md`**: `DailyBoard.test.tsx` is now in `proven_in`.
- **Tests**:
  - `DailyBoard.test.tsx` has a new case. A sequence question on the daily board shows `prompt-streak` and `daily-clock`, and no `prompt-sequence-clock`.
  - `PromptE18.test.tsx` has a new case. A live sequence question shows the countdown with a `data-seconds` attribute, and none when `sequenceClock={false}`.
  - `renderPrompt` in that file now takes an optional `sequenceClock`.

## How I tested it
- `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/daily/DailyBoard.test.tsx src/game/PromptE18.test.tsx src/game/Prompt.test.tsx`: 3 files and 110 tests passed. I had to run `sh scripts/build-wasm.sh` first, because the wasm package was missing.
- I replaced `sequenceClock={false}` in `DailyBoard.tsx` with a comment and re-ran `DailyBoard.test.tsx`. The new case failed (1 failed, 17 passed). I restored the line afterwards.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` and `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/game apps/web/src/daily` were clean.
- `cargo fmt --check` was clean.
- `cargo jackioh spec check` printed `2182 rulings, 5547 proofs, 69636 citations in 4541 files, 29293 links: ok`.

## Decisions
- **Hide the countdown, rather than show the daily clock in its place.** The issue allowed either. `DailyClockPill` is already on the board, so a second clock inside the prompt would repeat it.
- **Fallback only.** When no `sequenceClock` prop is passed, the countdown shows. Only `DailyBoard` passes false.
- **Departure from the plan.** None.

## For the reviewer
Only the engine `<PromptModal>` in `Prompt` receives the prop. The `source="play"` modal does not, because a play's picker never has a sequence.

Built and checked on `claude-8`. This is a draft while its own review run, on the same subscription, reviews it adversarially and fixes what it finds (up to 3 rounds); CI runs on it meanwhile. Once that review approves it, it is marked ready and auto-merge turns on.

# #3839: Patch: the daily board shows no 60-second countdown on KY's Competition's questions
Opened by @jgoetzmann.

A follow-up to daily games (#3727, merged in #3762), found in its review and left out of it. Part of the tracker #3726.

### What happens

R3727003 says a daily game's question sequence for KY's Competition (Meditative+ #20) has no 60-second window: the move's own deadline is its window, and the server keeps no clock of seconds. The daily board still shows the live game's countdown on those questions, "Time left: 60 s" ticking down. Nothing enforces it, so reaching 0 does nothing; it only tells the player something false.

- [`apps/web/src/game/Prompt.tsx:819`](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/blob/1964004112/apps/web/src/game/Prompt.tsx#L819-L828): `SequenceCountdown` always calls `useSequenceSecondsLeft` (`apps/web/src/game/sequenceClock.ts`), and the picker renders it on every sequence question ([line 1383](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/blob/1964004112/apps/web/src/game/Prompt.tsx#L1383)).
- [`apps/web/src/daily/DailyBoard.tsx`](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/blob/1964004112/apps/web/src/daily/DailyBoard.tsx) renders the ordinary `Game.tsx`, which renders `Prompt`, with nothing telling it the game is a daily one.

### What should happen

On the daily board a KY's Competition question shows no 60-second countdown (R3727003). It may show the move's daily clock instead (`DailyClockPill.tsx`). A live match and practice keep the 60 seconds (R1563006).

### How to reproduce

Start a daily game (two friends; Challenge, then Daily), play Meditative+ #20 KY's Competition, and look at its first question: `prompt-sequence-clock` is shown and counts down from 60.

### Fix

Let `DailyBoard` tell `Game`, and through it `Prompt`, not to show the sequence countdown (a prop), or to show the daily clock in its place. Add a case to `apps/web/src/daily/DailyBoard.test.tsx`: a KY's Competition question on the daily board shows no `prompt-sequence-clock`. The case must fail without the fix. Keep the live game's own test of the countdown passing.

On the daily board (`DailyBoard`), a KY's Competition (Meditative+ #20) question shows no 60-second countdown, so `prompt-sequence-clock` is absent (R3727003). The move's daily clock pill (`DailyClockPill`) is already on the board, so nothing replaces the countdown. A live match and practice keep the countdown (R1563006). Do it with one boolean prop passed from `DailyBoard` through `Game` and `Prompt` to the sequence picker. Add a daily-board test that fails without the fix, and a test that the live prompt still shows the countdown.

| Path | Change |
|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/game/Prompt.tsx` | `change`: add the optional `sequenceClock` prop to `PromptProps` and `PromptModal`. Gate the `SequenceCountdown` render on it. Pass it from `Prompt` to the engine `PromptModal`. |
| `apps/web/src/game/Game.tsx` | `change`: add the optional `sequenceClock` prop to `GameProps` (default `true`) and pass it to `<Prompt>`. |

| `apps/web/src/daily/DailyBoard.test.tsx` | `change`: add the daily-board case. |

Change the condition to `readOnly || !sequenceClock || picker.streak === undefined || picker.sequenceChoice === undefined ? null : (<SequenceCountdown …/>)`. `SequenceCountdown` and `useSequenceSecondsLeft` stay unchanged, so no hook is called conditionally.    - In `GameProps`, beside `endTurnLabel` (line ~194), add `/** R3727003: false on a daily game's board: its question sequence shows no 60-second countdown. */ sequenceClock?: boolean;`.

## Tests

**`apps/web/src/daily/DailyBoard.test.tsx`**, inside `describe("#3727 a daily game's board", …)`. Add the import `pendingFor` to the existing `../test/fixtures.ts` import line.
- `it("R3727003 a KY's Competition question shows no 60-second countdown, only the move's daily clock", async () => { … })`:
  - Build the game with `dailyGame({ view: baseView({ pending: pendingFor("answer", [{ key: "mode:A", label: "285" }, { key: "mode:B", label: "295" }, { key: "none", label: "Stop" }], { prompt: "482 − 197 = ?", streak: 0 }) }), legal: [] })`.
  - Mirror the `PendingOption` shape and the `streak` field exactly as `PromptE18.test.tsx`'s `sequenceView` does.
  - Serve it with `serve(() => game)` and `render(<DailyBoard matchId="g-1" />)`.
  - `await screen.findByTestId("prompt-streak", undefined, SLOW)`, which proves the sequence question is open.
  - Assert `screen.queryByTestId("prompt-sequence-clock")` is `null`.
  - Assert `screen.getByTestId(dailyTestid.clock)` is present.
  - If `legal: []` hides the prompt, copy the `legal` shape other daily tests use for a pending choice.

**`apps/web/src/game/PromptE18.test.tsx`**, inside `describe("a question sequence (Meditative+ #20 KY's Competition)")`:
- `it("R1563006 a question of a sequence shows its 60-second countdown, and none where sequenceClock is false", …)`:
  - `renderPrompt(sequenceView(0))`, then assert `screen.getByTestId("prompt-sequence-clock")` is present and has a `data-seconds` attribute.
  - `cleanup()`, then render `<Prompt view={sequenceView(0)} legal={[]} onAction={vi.fn()} sequenceClock={false} />` inside the same providers `renderPrompt` uses (copy them from `renderPrompt`, line 38 of that file). Assert `queryByTestId("prompt-sequence-clock")` is `null` and `prompt-streak` is still shown.
  - Before writing it, check whether `renderPrompt` accepts extra props. If it does not, add an optional `sequenceClock?: boolean` to its props object and spread it in.

Commands:
- `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/daily/DailyBoard.test.tsx src/game/PromptE18.test.tsx src/game/Prompt.test.tsx`
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`
- `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/game apps/web/src/daily`
- `cargo jackioh spec check`

To confirm the daily test fails without the fix, temporarily remove `sequenceClock={false}` from `DailyBoard.tsx`, run that file and see the new case fail, then restore it.

## Done when

- [ ] The daily board shows no `prompt-sequence-clock` on a KY's Competition question, and the clock pill is still there.
- [ ] A live `Prompt`, and `Game` without the prop, still show the countdown (the new `PromptE18` case).
- [ ] The new `DailyBoard` case fails with `sequenceClock={false}` removed, and passes with it.
- [ ] `Prompt.test.tsx`, `PromptE18.test.tsx` and `DailyBoard.test.tsx` pass.
- [ ] Web typecheck and eslint are clean, with no `eslint-disable` or `@ts-ignore`.
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo jackioh spec check` pass.
- [ ] No file outside the table changed.

## Risks

- Other `Game` and `Prompt` callers (practice, hotseat, online, tutorial, dungeon) must keep the countdown. The prop defaults to true, and only `DailyBoard` passes false.
- Replays are already read-only, with no countdown, so nothing changes there.
- `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` may be on (the file spreads optional props conditionally). Passing `sequenceClock={…}` as a boolean is fine, but never pass `undefined` explicitly.
- `sequenceStartedAt` in `sequenceClock.ts` holds module state, and a test in the same file may leave an open sequence. The live test only asserts the element exists, not the exact seconds, so this doesn't matter.

## Open questions

None. The issue allows either hiding the countdown or showing the daily clock in its place. I chose to hide it, because `DailyClockPill` is already on the board and a second clock inside the prompt would repeat it.
